title: Baby found 'emaciated' 19 days after social services closed case

evidence_packet.title: Baby found 'emaciated' 19 days after social services closed case
evidence_packet.lead: The girl was covered in sores, severely dehydrated and had "paper-thin skin" when she was treated
evidence_packet.summary: The girl was covered in sores, severely dehydrated and had "paper-thin skin" when she was treated
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Baby found 'emaciated' 19 days after social services closed case - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, The 19-month-old girl was less than half the weight a child should be on average for her age By Jonny Humphries North West Published 2 hours ago An "incredibly emaciated" and starving baby, covered in sores, was taken to hospital in a critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, a review has found. The 19-month-old girl weighed 9.7lb (4.4kg) - less than half the 24lb (11kg) expected for an average child of her age - when she was treated in February 2025. A Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, reported the girl was severely dehydrated, had no fatty tissue noted on her body and had "paper-thin skin". The case was closed despite warnings her mother, who was 17 when the baby was born, was neglecting her daughter and had avoided social workers and health visitors for weeks. The CSPR, which referred to the girl as Child K1, said she displayed "skin breakdown" across the "entirety" of her bottom and nappy area. Expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall said medics found "wasting to the buttocks" and open pressure sores extending along her back, hips and bottom. She wrote: "Child K1's presentation of hypothermia, hypoglycaemia [low blood sugar], severe malnutrition, dehydration along with renal failure, evidenced by severe abnormality of blood salts, could have led to death if it had not been identified and emergency treatment initiated." Anonymous tip The review found the baby's mother had struggled with anxiety and low mood since the birth, and had been relying heavily on her own mother to care for the child. title: New PM brings new hope for justice, nuclear tests veteran says

evidence_packet.title: New PM brings new hope for justice, nuclear tests veteran says
evidence_packet.lead: John Morris, who saw nuclear tests in the 1950s, says Andy Burnham backs an independent inquiry
evidence_packet.summary: John Morris, who saw nuclear tests in the 1950s, says Andy Burnham backs an independent inquiry
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who was exposed to nuclear tests in the 1950s has said Andy Burnham has finally given him "hope" of getting justice John Morris, of Rochdale, Greater Manchester, was 18 when he was sent to Christmas Island in the Pacific, where bombs were detonated in a series of infamous tests conducted by the Ministry of Defence (MoD) Many veterans suffered serious medical problems afterwards and have now called for the new prime minister to fast-track an independent inquiry Burnham has repeatedly backed their cause after some of the 22,000 military personnel claimed they were used as guinea pigs but the MoD said compensation is available through the War Pensions Scheme Now 88, Morris is part of a group of veterans who have lodged a criminal complaint against the Ministry of Defence (MoD) saying they are "devastated at the way veterans are being denied justice" But it is Burnham's appointment that has given Morris hope as he claims the PM backs a judicial review

title: What is Jodrell Bank Observatory and what does it do?

evidence_packet.title: What is Jodrell Bank Observatory and what does it do?
evidence_packet.lead: When Jodrell Bank Observatory was built, the site was seen as gamechanger for radio astronomy
evidence_packet.summary: When Jodrell Bank Observatory was built, the site was seen as gamechanger for radio astronomy
evidence_packet.evidence_text: All scientific work carried out using the UK's largest telescope could end in the next two years The government has decided to pull funding for the Jodrell Bank Observatory to focus investment on projects that deliver long-term impact It has left the University of Manchester, which owns the site in Cheshire, scrambling to find alternative cash before 2028 Astronomers have described the move as "short-sighted" and a significant blow to the UK's research capabilities The observatory is a Unesco World Heritage Site and stands between two villages in the east of rural Cheshire on a site that spans less than one square mile It is dominated by the enormous Lovell Telescope and its 250ft (76m) wide dish, which can be seen 20 miles (32km) away in Manchester

title: The 1% Club winner breaks world record for eating fish fingers

evidence_packet.title: The 1% Club winner breaks world record for eating fish fingers
evidence_packet.lead: Nathan Davies, 32, promised to break a world record when he was a contestant on The 1% Club
evidence_packet.summary: Nathan Davies, 32, promised to break a world record when he was a contestant on The 1% Club
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man has broken a world record for eating 15 fish fingers in 60 seconds - after making the promise on a gameshow Nathan Davies, 32, from Westhoughton, Bolton, claimed the Guinness World Records title for scoffing the most fish fingers in a minute after vowing to do so to Lee Mack, the host of ITV's The 1% Club The dad of two, who took home £98,000 after winning the show, said he "always has 20 fish fingers in the freezer, so I thought, that one sounds achievable" Davies said he believed he could have eaten more if he had been able to let them cool down, adding: "I'm just happy to have the record." title: Wigan's new market plans do not have enough stalls, traders say

evidence_packet.title: Wigan's new market plans do not have enough stalls, traders say
evidence_packet.lead: There are currently 35 traders on Wigan market, but the new indoor hall will only have 21 stalls
evidence_packet.summary: There are currently 35 traders on Wigan market, but the new indoor hall will only have 21 stalls
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new indoor market hall in Greater Manchester will not have enough stalls, several of its traders have complained There are about 35 stallholders at the existing Wigan indoor market hall and they have been told there will not be enough room for them all to relocate next spring into a new building in the town's flagship Fettlers development Jonathan Lamb, who has run his JL Jewellers watch repair business for 33 years, said: "The council has said there will be 21 stalls in the new building and we've been told we have to apply for one, so it's like a knife in the back." Aidan Thatcher, director for place at Wigan Council, said: "The feedback we have received is now being actively considered." He said: "We have been engaging with traders on unit numbers, space requirements, and the balance between trading and complementary uses." Lamb, 60, told BBC Radio Manchester: "I'm very optimistic about the new market hall and we've been promised the world by Wigan Council but we're not guaranteed anything

title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll

evidence_packet.title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll
evidence_packet.lead: Why the Supplementary Vote may allow voters to vote with their heads and their hearts
evidence_packet.summary: Why the Supplementary Vote may allow voters to vote with their heads and their hearts
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV comes into replace the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system used at the last election A number of candidates have already declared for the contest , triggered after Andy Burnham's successful campaign to become the MP of Makerfield, leaving the post he has held since 2017 vacant Prof Jonathan Tonge of the University of Liverpool said Labour could pick up second preference votes from Greens and Lib Dems, while Reform could be less likely to see Restore voters put them as second preference due to "bad blood" between the party leaders The system was used in the first two mayoral elections, but was scrapped by the last Conservative government in favour of FPTP system, before it was reintroduced again by Labour Under SV, candidates need to win more than 50% of the vote in the first round to be come mayor or the top two candidates go into a run-off where second preference votes from eliminated candidates are counted

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they will be fighting for? evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wildfires across Greater Manchester are still burning a fortnight after they first started, the fire service has said More than 100 firefighters and volunteers have been tackling the blaze on two fronts at Dove Stone, after the fire in Saddleworth merged with a fire at Tintwistle, and at Swineshaw Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said specialists from across the UK had been drafted in to control any remaining hotspots The fires in Greater Manchester and Derbyshire have burned hundreds of hectares of moorland, equivalent to the size of 1,250 football pitches, the landowner has said The fire service said light rainfall and mist had dampened the moorlands, but the fires had not been extinguished It said the fires were still being classed as a "major incident"

title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife

evidence_packet.title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife
evidence_packet.lead: A World War Two air raid shelter has been turned into a haven for wildlife with Trafford Council calling the work 'inspirational'
evidence_packet.summary: A World War Two air raid shelter has been turned into a haven for wildlife with Trafford Council calling the work 'inspirational'
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters and drinking stations for insects and animals beside it Work at the site in Urmston, Greater Manchester, has been made possible with the help of local businesses "It's been absolutely thriving with wildlife, said Lisa Smith, allotment treasurer. "We've even had a fox up there. It's just been such an incredible achievement to create this." Smith added: "Since World War Two, pollinators have been under threat due to the loss of 97 per cent of wildflower meadows in the UK, so we thought we really need to try and rectify that." Mick Heery, chairman of Brookfield Allotment, told BBC Radio Manchester sustainability also plays an important role in their work

evidence_packet.evidence_text: An "incredibly emaciated" and starving baby, covered in sores, was taken to hospital in a critical condition 19 days after social services closed her case, a review has found The 19-month-old girl weighed 9.7lb (4.4kg) - less than half the 24lb (11kg) expected for an average child of her age - when she was treated in February 2025 A Child Safeguarding Practice Review (CSPR) in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, reported the girl was severely dehydrated, had no fatty tissue noted on her body and had "paper-thin skin" The case was closed despite warnings her mother, who was 17 when the baby was born, was neglecting her daughter and had avoided social workers and health visitors for weeks The CSPR, which referred to the girl as Child K1, said she displayed "skin breakdown" across the "entirety" of her bottom and nappy area Expert reviewer Nicki Walker-Hall said medics found "wasting to the buttocks" and open pressure sores extending along her back, hips and bottom

evidence_packet.evidence_text: All scientific work carried out using the UK's largest telescope could end in the next two years The government has decided to pull funding for the Jodrell Bank Observatory to focus investment on projects that deliver long-term impact It has left the University of Manchester, which owns the site in Cheshire, scrambling to find alternative cash before 2028 Astronomers have described the move as "short-sighted" and a significant blow to the UK's research capabilities The observatory is a Unesco World Heritage Site and stands between two villages in the east of rural Cheshire on a site that spans less than one square mile It is dominated by the enormous Lovell Telescope and its 250ft (76m) wide dish, which can be seen 20 miles (32km) away in Manchester

title: Wigan's new market plans do not have enough stalls, traders say

evidence_packet.title: Wigan's new market plans do not have enough stalls, traders say
evidence_packet.lead: A new indoor market hall in Greater Manchester will not have enough stalls, several of its traders have complained There are about 35 stallholders at the existing Wigan indoor market hall and they have been told there will not be enough room for them all to relocate next spring i
evidence_packet.summary: A new indoor market hall in Greater Manchester will not have enough stalls, several of its traders have complained There are about 35 stallholders at the existing Wigan indoor market hall and they have been told there will not be enough room for them all to relocate next spring i
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new indoor market hall in Greater Manchester will not have enough stalls, several of its traders have complained There are about 35 stallholders at the existing Wigan indoor market hall and they have been told there will not be enough room for them all to relocate next spring into a new building in the town's flagship Fettlers development Jonathan Lamb, who has run his JL Jewellers watch repair business for 33 years, said: "The council has said there will be 21 stalls in the new building and we've been told we have to apply for one, so it's like a knife in the back." Aidan Thatcher, director for place at Wigan Council, said: "The feedback we have received is now being actively considered." He said: "We have been engaging with traders on unit numbers, space requirements, and the balance between trading and complementary uses." Lamb, 60, told BBC Radio Manchester: "I'm very optimistic about the new market hall and we've been promised the world by Wigan Council but we're not guaranteed anything

title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll

evidence_packet.title: Why voting method change matters in mayoral poll
evidence_packet.lead: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV c
evidence_packet.summary: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV c
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Labour Party could benefit most from the return of the supplementary votes (SV) system in the Greater Manchester mayoral race, a polling expert has said Voters in the region head to the polls on 30 July and will be able to select a first and second choice of candidate as SV comes into replace the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system used at the last election A number of candidates have already declared for the contest , triggered after Andy Burnham's successful campaign to become the MP of Makerfield, leaving the post he has held since 2017 vacant Prof Jonathan Tonge of the University of Liverpool said Labour could pick up second preference votes from Greens and Lib Dems, while Reform could be less likely to see Restore voters put them as second preference due to "bad blood" between the party leaders The system was used in the first two mayoral elections, but was scrapped by the last Conservative government in favour of FPTP system, before it was reintroduced again by Labour Under SV, candidates need to win more than 50% of the vote in the first round to be come mayor or the top two candidates go into a run-off where second preference votes from eliminated candidates are counted

title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?

evidence_packet.title: What is the Greater Manchester mayor and what do they do?
evidence_packet.lead: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they wil
evidence_packet.summary: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they wil
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Andy Burnham's victory in the Makerfield by-election means he has to step down as Greater Manchester mayor Burnham has been mayor since the role was first created in 2017 and the race to become his successor will be fiercely contested by all involved But what is the role they will be fighting for? The role of mayor was created as part of a law passed in 2016, one of a number of big pieces of devolution legislation brought in by the Conservatives after taking power in 2010 In a 2012 referendum, Manchester rejected having a directly-elected city mayor, along with eight other major cities, but the decision to have a regional or metropolitan mayor was directly negotiated between the government and the 10 Greater Manchester councils Andy Burnham, who left Parliament to stand for the role, was chosen as Labour's candidate for the first mayoral election in 2017 and won, taking 63.4% of the vote

title: Moorland wildfires in Greater Manchester still burning a fortnight on

evidence_packet.title: Moorland wildfires in Greater Manchester still burning a fortnight on
evidence_packet.lead: Wildfires across Greater Manchester are still burning a fortnight after they first started, the fire service has said More than 100 firefighters and volunteers have been tackling the blaze on two fronts at Dove Stone, after the fire in Saddleworth merged with a fire at Tintwistle
evidence_packet.summary: Wildfires across Greater Manchester are still burning a fortnight after they first started, the fire service has said More than 100 firefighters and volunteers have been tackling the blaze on two fronts at Dove Stone, after the fire in Saddleworth merged with a fire at Tintwistle
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wildfires across Greater Manchester are still burning a fortnight after they first started, the fire service has said More than 100 firefighters and volunteers have been tackling the blaze on two fronts at Dove Stone, after the fire in Saddleworth merged with a fire at Tintwistle, and at Swineshaw Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said specialists from across the UK had been drafted in to control any remaining hotspots The fires in Greater Manchester and Derbyshire have burned hundreds of hectares of moorland, equivalent to the size of 1,250 football pitches, the landowner has said The fire service said light rainfall and mist had dampened the moorlands, but the fires had not been extinguished It said the fires were still being classed as a "major incident"

title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife

evidence_packet.title: Trafford WW2 bunker transformed to help wildlife
evidence_packet.lead: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters
evidence_packet.summary: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters
evidence_packet.evidence_text: An air raid shelter that once protected families from bombs during World War Two has been turned into a haven for wildlife including birds, insects and hedgehogs Plot holders at Brookfield Allotment have planted a wildflower garden on the roof of the bunker and installed shelters and drinking stations for insects and animals beside it Work at the site in Urmston, Greater Manchester, has been made possible with the help of local businesses "It's been absolutely thriving with wildlife, said Lisa Smith, allotment treasurer. "We've even had a fox up there. It's just been such an incredible achievement to create this." Smith added: "Since World War Two, pollinators have been under threat due to the loss of 97 per cent of wildflower meadows in the UK, so we thought we really need to try and rectify that." Mick Heery, chairman of Brookfield Allotment, told BBC Radio Manchester sustainability also plays an important role in their work

evidence_packet.lead: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bi
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bike ran a red light before ploughed into a mum crossing the road her young child in a pram Bradley Price, 19, said he was rushing to see his friend when his brakes failed and he hit with the mother and her four-year-old son at a pedestrian crossing in Middleton They were were taken to hospital and treated for their injuries. The child suffered a head laceration, which needed surgery, as did the mother Price was travelling along Long Street away from Middleton town centre on an adapted e-bike - which could reach speeds of up to 70 miles per hour due to its modified throttle - wearing a balaclava, Minshull Street Crown Court heard The incident, on February 10, has left mum victim with severe anxiety. Her son has lost confidence, the court heard. The mum said: "We have both been left with permanent scars. I have a scar on my eye which is a permanent reminder of what happened

evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport is 'overwhelmed' with people 'making it a mess' by lighting barbecues and littering during recent heatwaves Reddish Vale Country park spans 161 hectares along the River Tame in the heart of Stockport . It provides a green corridor linking the town centre with Denton in Tameside, and Woodley The 'lovely park' with 'great views' is a popular destination for people providing access to nature. Part of the site is a designated local nature reserve. It is managed by Stockport council One person living in the area said police have been called due to people lighting fires and barbecues during periods of hot weather wasting police time amid safety concerns. There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manch A public question was raised by Angela Dennerley during a Stockport Council Reddish area committee on July 27 who asked what the council was doing to address issues at the Reddish Vale Country Park

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Terrifying moment cops tackled screaming knifeman on school grounds Both Douk Deng was said to be 'frustrated' that his asylum claim had been refused Comments News Press Association , Amy Walker Court reporter and Greta Simpson Senior Reporte Local cops were called to the Edgar Wood Academy in Middleton on August 6 last year after a staff member reported a suspicious man on the grounds of the school, at which no children were present as it was the summer holidays Body cam footage shared by Greater Manchester Police shows officers jumping from the car and running at Both Douk Deng, 21, ordering him to stop There is a brief scuffle before the officers tackle Deng to the ground as he screams. They can be heard remarking that he has a hammer and a hatchet with him Both Douk Deng was jailed for two years today (July 28) after pleading guilty to a range of offences including criminal damage and possessing weapons and a knife in a public place and on school premises Deng had become 'increasingly frustrated' that immigration authorities were not providing assistance in his bid to stay and work in the UK

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Science 'The next generation needs to be inspired': Sadness at Jodrell Bank as visitors take in magnificence of under-threat Lovell Telescope The Manchester Evening News has launched a campaign to secure the future of the Lovell Telescope, where all s News Ludwik Lipiec Apprentice content creator 06:00, 29 Jul 2026 A long, proud history of groundbreaking research and space exploration at Jodrell Bank Observatory is under threat. Unless new funding for the iconic landmark is found, it could all be over in just 20 months from no The Manchester Evening News has launched a campaign to secure the future of the Lovell Telescope, where all scientific observations could cease after financial backing for the e-Merlin telescope network - around £2.8m a year - was axed Politicians have slammed the move, saying scientific excellence has been 'stripped' from the north for decades in favour of the 'golden triangle' cluster of elite universities of the south and London The Macclesfield observatory's Jodrell Bank Centre for Engagement - hugely popular for educational school trips - is not affected and would remain open. It is the science that would be lost without a new funding being found Macclesfield locals and visitors spoke of their sadness at the prospect of research ending when the Manchester Evening News visited

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Firefighters scrambled to Turkish Airlines flight after it diverts to Manchester Airport It is understood the flight landed safely Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 22:06, 28 Jul 2026 Updated 22:07, 28 Jul 2026 View 2 Imag A Turkish Airlines flight was forced to divert to Manchester Airport today (July 28) Flight THY1GJ travelling from Istanbul to Toronto made the landing at around 7:30pm after doing some laps over the North Sea, potentially ditching fuel to allow it to land, according to flight data Several fire engines were at the scene and spotted heading towards the aircraft after it landed at Manchester View 2 Images The Toronto-bound plane made an emergency landing (Image: Liam Smith ) A spokesperson for Manchester Airport said the aircraft had landed safely and had a 'technical issue' that had since been resolved

evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 The next mayor's in-tray: The seven maps that show the challenges facing Andy Burnham's successor Andy Burnham leaves behind a city region that is wealthier, more influential and more powerful than it was eight News Rob Williams Features a
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 The next mayor's in-tray: The seven maps that show the challenges facing Andy Burnham's successor Andy Burnham leaves behind a city region that is wealthier, more influential and more powerful than it was eight News Rob Williams Features a
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 The next mayor's in-tray: The seven maps that show the challenges facing Andy Burnham's successor Andy Burnham leaves behind a city region that is wealthier, more influential and more powerful than it was eight News Rob Williams Features and Perspectives Editor and David Dubas-Fisher-MEN 19:05, 28 Jul 2026 Whoever walks into Greater Manchester’s mayoral office on Friday evening will inherit one of the most influential jobs outside Westminster. Eight years ago, the role was still somethi It’s the office that propelled Andy Burnham from regional politics and into Downing Street His successor will quickly discover that the title comes with formidable expectations. The next mayor will be expected to tackle homelessness, improve public transport, unlock thousands of new homes, attract investment, reduce inequality and convince residents that prosperity is They will attempt to do all this against the backdrop of one of the closest mayoral elections Greater Manchester has yet seen, with Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK’s Sian Astley leading the race and a second round of counting expected for the first time under the Supplementary V Under Supplementary Vote, people cast both a first and second preference. If no candidate wins more than 50 per cent of first preferences (which Burnham always did), all but the top two candidates are eliminated before second preference votes are redistributed

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires 60 personnel still battling Tintwistle Moor fire as 'major incident' remains The blaze began almost three weeks ago Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:47, 28 Jul 2026 View 2 Images A view of a section of the Tintwistle moor fire (Ima Around 60 people have been battling the Tintwistle Moor fires today (July 28) more than three weeks on from the start of the blaze A major incident was declared in the area on July 12 after the blaze broke out on July 9 - following an earlier fire which crews tackled from June 24 to July 2 Today Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service said they were 'continuing to make progress' on the blaze but that it remained a 'complex' and 'challenging' incident, asking the public to not ignore road closures and continue to take precautions to prevent further fires They also said that Woodhead Pass (A628) remained closed and would do until at least tomorrow (July 29) The road between Hollingworth and Flouch has been closed since July 16 after a dramatic car fire broke out and spread to the nearby moors

evidence_packet.lead: Courts Four men on trial accused of murdering Alexander John Soyoye, 16, amid 'clash with rival gang' fled UK in wake of killing, jurors told Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga and Emerson Teta deny murdering Alexander John Soyoye News Amy W Four men on trial accused of
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Four men on trial accused of murdering Alexander John Soyoye, 16, amid 'clash with rival gang' fled UK in wake of killing, jurors told Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga and Emerson Teta deny murdering Alexander John Soyoye News Amy W Four men on trial accused of
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Four men on trial accused of murdering Alexander John Soyoye, 16, amid 'clash with rival gang' fled UK in wake of killing, jurors told Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga and Emerson Teta deny murdering Alexander John Soyoye News Amy W Four men on trial accused of murdering a 16-year-old boy amid a 'clash with a rival gang' fled the country in the wake of the killing, a jury has heard Alexander John Soyoye, also known as John, lost his life on November 5, 2020. It came, jurors heard, amid a feud between the Moston based 'M40' gang and the Rochdale and Oldham outfit Representing the Danger (RTD). Prosecutors said hostilities spilled onto the streets of Moston Manchester Crown Court heard the stabbing of a relative of an M40 gang member in Piccadilly Gardens earlier that day was the catalyst for a brutal 'revenge' attack which resulted in Mr Soyoye's death hours later Jurors heard RTD members later headed to Moston to 'exact revenge', with the groups involved in a violent melee. M40 gang members became overwhelmed and fled, it was said Mr Soyoye was injured in the earlier fight, jurors heard. He became isolated before being punched, kicked and stabbed, the court heard, suffering 15 blows to his body. Mr Soyoye, the trial heard, died at the scene

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The Ghost, Rocket Ronnie and a 17-year-old boy: The dealers who revived Rochdale's notorious £1m-a-year 'Adam' drugs line It was first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG View 3 Images Haider Ali, left, and Alan Ronald News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:27, 28 Jul 2026 Updated 17:28, 28 Jul 2026 Two drug dealers have been sentenced for their part in a notorious Rochdale drugs line which survived despite a series of police operations to bring it down In 2024 two 'untouchable' drug dealers were the latest to be jailed for running the 'Adam Line', first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG which shone a light on the gang based in Newbold, Rochdale. Members of the gang were shown to bribe witnesses, groom But the drugs line became active again within hours of the pair being arrested. In its latest incarnation, Haider Ali, 34, who was known as 'The Ghost', was running the infamous drugs line, until he and two others were caught by police last year. Now they have been brought to jus When a CCTV operator spotted what appeared to be a drug deal in progress on Baron Street in Rochdale, officers followed a Nissan Qashqai car and when they swooped Ali ran away from the front passenger seat but was arrested a short distance away He had £1,000 in cash on him as well as wraps of cocaine and heroin in his pockets. On the dashboard in front of his seat police found 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Brave woman sexually abused as a child faces remorseless predator who put her through two trials 'Not once have you acknowledged what you did, let alone apologised. Even now, that lack of accountability hurts deeply and amplifies the fear that A predator who sexually abused a young girl has faced justice decades on Malkiat Rai is behind bars following crimes he committed against a child in the 1990s. His victim faced him in court, telling him: "What you did did not affect one moment of my childhood - it affected the course of my entire life." Malkiat Rai was in his mid-20s at the time, Manchester Crown Court heard. His brother Jaswant Singh Rai was jailed for three years and 10 months in 2024 in relation to offences against the same victim - five counts of indecent assault; and one count of indecency with a child. He As Malkiat Rai, 59, from Salford, was jailed for seven-and-a-half years, the victim spoke of the pain that has 'followed' her, saying it 'continues to affect [her] every single day' Malkiat Rai went on trial in 2023, but jurors could not reach verdicts on the counts he faced. He faced a sentencing hearing this week having been found guilty of four counts of indecent assault; and two counts of indecency with a child following a retrial earlier this month

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Animals A 31-year-old cat lives in Stockport, her owner has revealed the secret to her long life Stockport resident Leslie Greenhough claims to have the world's oldest cat Comments News Miranda Pell Search and Discover Writer 17:16, 28 Jul 2026 View 4 A man who claims to have the world's oldest cat has revealed his secret to giving his furry friend a long, healthy life Leslie Greenhough, 71, from Stockport, believes his tortoiseshell Millie, born in 1995, is currently the oldest living feline at the age of 31 , which for cats is the equivalent of 146 human years Millie was first owned by Leslie's late wife, Paula, who got Millie the same year as a three-month-old kitten. Paula sadly died aged 55 in 2020 Leslie has since said Millie's incredible lifespan is down to feeding her only Buxton natural mineral water for the past decade - alongside "lots of treats" including "cuddles on the sofa" View 4 Images Leslie says her longevity to partly down to her only drinking Buxton spring water (Image: SWNS)

The alert is in place from Tuesday to Thursday, and the agency warned that rising temperatures may increase health risks, particularly for v Temperatures are expected to peak as high as 35C across south-east England. But it will feel slightly cooler in Greater Manchester today with highs of 24C expected today amid sunny and cloudy conditions Highs of 20C and 21C are then expected in our region in the following days with more sunny intervals. Amid the current heatwave, experts have warned wildfires could be 'exceptionally severe' by Wednesday if they start in parts of London, the South East and eastern England, as a r Fire and rescue services in England and Wales have responded to 706 wildfires so far in 2026, with 208 incidents recorded between July 16 and 28 alone, the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The £20k 'Mortgage Man' fraudster who 'took victims for a ride' 'In reality, Francis had no financial qualifications, and he used the cash for his own personal gain' Comments News Gary Porter and Paul Britton Reporter 07:53, 29 Jul 2026 View Im A con artist posed as a mortgage advisor to dupe four people out of more than £200,000 Adam Francis, 48, offered his services as the 'Mortgage Man', but police said the 'cunning and deceitful' fraudster had no formal financial qualifications. evidence_packet.title: Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance'
evidence_packet.lead: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bi
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bike ran a red light before ploughed into a mum crossing the road her young child in a pram Bradley Price, 19, said he was rushing to see his friend when his brakes failed and he hit with the mother and her four-year-old son at a pedestrian crossing in Middleton They were were taken to hospital and treated for their injuries. The child suffered a head laceration, which needed surgery, as did the mother Price was travelling along Long Street away from Middleton town centre on an adapted e-bike - which could reach speeds of up to 70 miles per hour due to its modified throttle - wearing a balaclava, Minshull Street Crown Court heard The incident, on February 10, has left mum victim with severe anxiety. Her son has lost confidence, the court heard. The mum said: "We have both been left with permanent scars. I have a scar on my eye which is a permanent reminder of what happened

title: Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park'

evidence_packet.title: Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park'
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport is 'overwhelmed' with people 'making it a mess' by lighting barbecues and littering during recent heatwaves Reddish Vale Country park spans 161 hectares along the River Tame in the heart of Stockport . It provides a green corridor linking the town centre with Denton in Tameside, and Woodley The 'lovely park' with 'great views' is a popular destination for people providing access to nature. Part of the site is a designated local nature reserve. It is managed by Stockport council One person living in the area said police have been called due to people lighting fires and barbecues during periods of hot weather wasting police time amid safety concerns. There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manch A public question was raised by Angela Dennerley during a Stockport Council Reddish area committee on July 27 who asked what the council was doing to address issues at the Reddish Vale Country Park

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rochdale Terrifying moment cops tackled screaming knifeman on school grounds Both Douk Deng was said to be 'frustrated' that his asylum claim had been refused Comments News Press Association , Amy Walker Court reporter and Greta Simpson Senior Reporte Local cops were called to the Edgar Wood Academy in Middleton on August 6 last year after a staff member reported a suspicious man on the grounds of the school, at which no children were present as it was the summer holidays Body cam footage shared by Greater Manchester Police shows officers jumping from the car and running at Both Douk Deng, 21, ordering him to stop There is a brief scuffle before the officers tackle Deng to the ground as he screams. They can be heard remarking that he has a hammer and a hatchet with him Both Douk Deng was jailed for two years today (July 28) after pleading guilty to a range of offences including criminal damage and possessing weapons and a knife in a public place and on school premises Deng had become 'increasingly frustrated' that immigration authorities were not providing assistance in his bid to stay and work in the UK

evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 The next mayor's in-tray: The seven maps that show the challenges facing Andy Burnham's successor Andy Burnham leaves behind a city region that is wealthier, more influential and more powerful than it was eight News Rob Williams Features a
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 The next mayor's in-tray: The seven maps that show the challenges facing Andy Burnham's successor Andy Burnham leaves behind a city region that is wealthier, more influential and more powerful than it was eight News Rob Williams Features a
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 The next mayor's in-tray: The seven maps that show the challenges facing Andy Burnham's successor Andy Burnham leaves behind a city region that is wealthier, more influential and more powerful than it was eight News Rob Williams Features and Perspectives Editor and David Dubas-Fisher-MEN 19:05, 28 Jul 2026 Whoever walks into Greater Manchester’s mayoral office on Friday evening will inherit one of the most influential jobs outside Westminster. Eight years ago, the role was still somethi It’s the office that propelled Andy Burnham from regional politics and into Downing Street His successor will quickly discover that the title comes with formidable expectations. The next mayor will be expected to tackle homelessness, improve public transport, unlock thousands of new homes, attract investment, reduce inequality and convince residents that prosperity is They will attempt to do all this against the backdrop of one of the closest mayoral elections Greater Manchester has yet seen, with Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK’s Sian Astley leading the race and a second round of counting expected for the first time under the Supplementary V Under Supplementary Vote, people cast both a first and second preference. If no candidate wins more than 50 per cent of first preferences (which Burnham always did), all but the top two candidates are eliminated before second preference votes are redistributed

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fires 60 personnel still battling Tintwistle Moor fire as 'major incident' remains The blaze began almost three weeks ago Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:47, 28 Jul 2026 View 2 Images A view of a section of the Tintwistle moor fire (Ima Around 60 people have been battling the Tintwistle Moor fires today (July 28) more than three weeks on from the start of the blaze A major incident was declared in the area on July 12 after the blaze broke out on July 9 - following an earlier fire which crews tackled from June 24 to July 2 Today Derbyshire Fire and Rescue Service said they were 'continuing to make progress' on the blaze but that it remained a 'complex' and 'challenging' incident, asking the public to not ignore road closures and continue to take precautions to prevent further fires They also said that Woodhead Pass (A628) remained closed and would do until at least tomorrow (July 29) The road between Hollingworth and Flouch has been closed since July 16 after a dramatic car fire broke out and spread to the nearby moors

evidence_packet.lead: Salford Two injured as man leads police on 45-minute chase at up to 100mph through Salford A 36-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:08, 28 Jul 2026 Updated 18:15, 28 Jul 2026 Greater Manchester Police sha
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Two injured as man leads police on 45-minute chase at up to 100mph through Salford A 36-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:08, 28 Jul 2026 Updated 18:15, 28 Jul 2026 Greater Manchester Police sha
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Two injured as man leads police on 45-minute chase at up to 100mph through Salford A 36-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:08, 28 Jul 2026 Updated 18:15, 28 Jul 2026 Greater Manchester Police shared the shocking footage which showed a black Nissan Qashqai travelling the wrong way up a carriageway, the wrong way around a roundabout and even onto grass verges to evade capture, after initially being asked to stop by the Tactical Vehicle Intercep Officers from the unit observed the car 'being driven dangerously and erratically' at high speeds and attempted to stop the vehicle in Salford at around 10:30am The driver then failed to stop, prompting a pursuit across the borough which reached up to speeds of 100mph and lasted for around 45 minutes, requiring multiple police vehicles and helicopters to intercept, the force said Helicopters from the National Police Air Service were deployed to aid the pursuit, which saw the vehicle travelling along the East Lancashire Road, against the flow of traffic around several roundabouts and through a Tesco car park View 2 Images The vehicle was seen travelling against the flow of traffic (Image: Greater Manchester Police )

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Education Andy Burnham announces bursaries and thousands of new college places announced in technical education shake-up 'For decades, young people have been told that desk jobs are the future' Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 16:10, 28 Jul The government is to roll out new bursaries and thousands of new college places to help encourage young people into technical education, training and apprenticeships, it has said Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced new and sweeping education reforms yesterday (July 28) which will establish routes for year 10 students to 'combine core academic subjects' with technical education, work experience and apprenticeships in their area It is also set to shake up the approach of Ofsted, with changes to the way schools are measured to 'increase recognition for places providing high-quality technical education' Today (July 28) the PM has gone further, announcing a new bursary for families on Universal Credit 'for whom the current system disincentivises apprenticeships' and pledging £287 million in funding to create 'over 22,000 new places' at colleges and post-16 training providers In a video clip posted on X, titled 'Can AI build a train?', he could be seen in a high-vis vest wielding a socket wrench as he set out his justification for the reforms

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester weather How hot it will be in Greater Manchester today as fourth heatwave of the year hits UK Some parts of the UK could see a peak temperatures of 35C on Wednesday News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 07:50, 29 Jul 2026 View Temperatures are set to reach 35C in some parts of the UK today (Wednesday, July 29) amid the fourth heatwave of the year An amber heat-health alert has been issued by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for the East Midlands, the East, South East and London. The alert is in place from Tuesday to Thursday, and the agency warned that rising temperatures may increase health risks, particularly for v Temperatures are expected to peak as high as 35C across south-east England. But it will feel slightly cooler in Greater Manchester today with highs of 24C expected today amid sunny and cloudy conditions Highs of 20C and 21C are then expected in our region in the following days with more sunny intervals. Amid the current heatwave, experts have warned wildfires could be 'exceptionally severe' by Wednesday if they start in parts of London, the South East and eastern England, as a r Fire and rescue services in England and Wales have responded to 706 wildfires so far in 2026, with 208 incidents recorded between July 16 and 28 alone, the National Fire Chiefs Council (NFCC) said

title: Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance'

evidence_packet.title: Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance'
evidence_packet.lead: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bi
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bi
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Masked teenager on e-bike who hit mum and young son after running red light given 'second chance' Bradley Price was riding his adapted e-bike when he ploughed into a mum and pram News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 06:32, 29 Jul 2026 View Image Brad A masked teenager on an e-bike ran a red light before ploughed into a mum crossing the road her young child in a pram Bradley Price, 19, said he was rushing to see his friend when his brakes failed and he hit with the mother and her four-year-old son at a pedestrian crossing in Middleton They were were taken to hospital and treated for their injuries. The child suffered a head laceration, which needed surgery, as did the mother Price was travelling along Long Street away from Middleton town centre on an adapted e-bike - which could reach speeds of up to 70 miles per hour due to its modified throttle - wearing a balaclava, Minshull Street Crown Court heard The incident, on February 10, has left mum victim with severe anxiety. Her son has lost confidence, the court heard. The mum said: "We have both been left with permanent scars. I have a scar on my eye which is a permanent reminder of what happened

evidence_packet.title: Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park'
evidence_packet.lead: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport
evidence_packet.summary: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Beauty spot 'overwhelmed' by mess as visitors slammed for destroying 'lovely park' There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manchester Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Re A country park in Stockport is 'overwhelmed' with people 'making it a mess' by lighting barbecues and littering during recent heatwaves Reddish Vale Country park spans 161 hectares along the River Tame in the heart of Stockport . It provides a green corridor linking the town centre with Denton in Tameside, and Woodley The 'lovely park' with 'great views' is a popular destination for people providing access to nature. Part of the site is a designated local nature reserve. It is managed by Stockport council One person living in the area said police have been called due to people lighting fires and barbecues during periods of hot weather wasting police time amid safety concerns. There have also been calls for tighter regulation following devastating fires in the moorlands above Manch A public question was raised by Angela Dennerley during a Stockport Council Reddish area committee on July 27 who asked what the council was doing to address issues at the Reddish Vale Country Park

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester mayoral election 2026 The next mayor's in-tray: The seven maps that show the challenges facing Andy Burnham's successor Andy Burnham leaves behind a city region that is wealthier, more influential and more powerful than it was eight News Rob Williams Features and Perspectives Editor and David Dubas-Fisher-MEN 19:05, 28 Jul 2026 Whoever walks into Greater Manchester’s mayoral office on Friday evening will inherit one of the most influential jobs outside Westminster. Eight years ago, the role was still somethi It’s the office that propelled Andy Burnham from regional politics and into Downing Street His successor will quickly discover that the title comes with formidable expectations. The next mayor will be expected to tackle homelessness, improve public transport, unlock thousands of new homes, attract investment, reduce inequality and convince residents that prosperity is They will attempt to do all this against the backdrop of one of the closest mayoral elections Greater Manchester has yet seen, with Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK’s Sian Astley leading the race and a second round of counting expected for the first time under the Supplementary V Under Supplementary Vote, people cast both a first and second preference. If no candidate wins more than 50 per cent of first preferences (which Burnham always did), all but the top two candidates are eliminated before second preference votes are redistributed

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Two injured as man leads police on 45-minute chase at up to 100mph through Salford A 36-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of dangerous driving Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 18:08, 28 Jul 2026 Updated 18:15, 28 Jul 2026 Greater Manchester Police shared the shocking footage which showed a black Nissan Qashqai travelling the wrong way up a carriageway, the wrong way around a roundabout and even onto grass verges to evade capture, after initially being asked to stop by the Tactical Vehicle Intercep Officers from the unit observed the car 'being driven dangerously and erratically' at high speeds and attempted to stop the vehicle in Salford at around 10:30am The driver then failed to stop, prompting a pursuit across the borough which reached up to speeds of 100mph and lasted for around 45 minutes, requiring multiple police vehicles and helicopters to intercept, the force said Helicopters from the National Police Air Service were deployed to aid the pursuit, which saw the vehicle travelling along the East Lancashire Road, against the flow of traffic around several roundabouts and through a Tesco car park View 2 Images The vehicle was seen travelling against the flow of traffic (Image: Greater Manchester Police )

Even now, that lack of accountability hurts deeply and amplifies the fear that A predator who sexually abused a young girl has faced justice decades on Malkiat Rai is behind bars following crimes he committed against a child in the 1990s. His victim faced him in court, telling him: "What you did did not affect one moment of my childhood - it affected the course of my entire life." Malkiat Rai was in his mid-20s at the time, Manchester Crown Court heard. His brother Jaswant Singh Rai was jailed for three years and 10 months in 2024 in relation to offences against the same victim - five counts of indecent assault; and one count of indecency with a child. He As Malkiat Rai, 59, from Salford, was jailed for seven-and-a-half years, the victim spoke of the pain that has 'followed' her, saying it 'continues to affect [her] every single day' Malkiat Rai went on trial in 2023, but jurors could not reach verdicts on the counts he faced. He faced a sentencing hearing this week having been found guilty of four counts of indecent assault; and two counts of indecency with a child following a retrial earlier this month

evidence_packet.lead: Courts Four men on trial accused of murdering Alexander John Soyoye, 16, amid 'clash with rival gang' fled UK in wake of killing, jurors told Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga and Emerson Teta deny murdering Alexander John Soyoye News Amy W Four men on trial accused of
evidence_packet.summary: Courts Four men on trial accused of murdering Alexander John Soyoye, 16, amid 'clash with rival gang' fled UK in wake of killing, jurors told Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga and Emerson Teta deny murdering Alexander John Soyoye News Amy W Four men on trial accused of
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Four men on trial accused of murdering Alexander John Soyoye, 16, amid 'clash with rival gang' fled UK in wake of killing, jurors told Ruben Candiza, Valdo De-Almeida, Marco Veiga and Emerson Teta deny murdering Alexander John Soyoye News Amy W Four men on trial accused of murdering a 16-year-old boy amid a 'clash with a rival gang' fled the country in the wake of the killing, a jury has heard Alexander John Soyoye, also known as John, lost his life on November 5, 2020. It came, jurors heard, amid a feud between the Moston based 'M40' gang and the Rochdale and Oldham outfit Representing the Danger (RTD). Prosecutors said hostilities spilled onto the streets of Moston Manchester Crown Court heard the stabbing of a relative of an M40 gang member in Piccadilly Gardens earlier that day was the catalyst for a brutal 'revenge' attack which resulted in Mr Soyoye's death hours later Jurors heard RTD members later headed to Moston to 'exact revenge', with the groups involved in a violent melee. M40 gang members became overwhelmed and fled, it was said Mr Soyoye was injured in the earlier fight, jurors heard. He became isolated before being punched, kicked and stabbed, the court heard, suffering 15 blows to his body. Mr Soyoye, the trial heard, died at the scene

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The Ghost, Rocket Ronnie and a 17-year-old boy: The dealers who revived Rochdale's notorious £1m-a-year 'Adam' drugs line It was first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG View 3 Images Haider Ali, left, and Alan Ronald News John Scheerhout Crime reporter 17:27, 28 Jul 2026 Updated 17:28, 28 Jul 2026 Two drug dealers have been sentenced for their part in a notorious Rochdale drugs line which survived despite a series of police operations to bring it down In 2024 two 'untouchable' drug dealers were the latest to be jailed for running the 'Adam Line', first exposed in the BBC series The Detectives: Taking Down An OCG which shone a light on the gang based in Newbold, Rochdale. Members of the gang were shown to bribe witnesses, groom But the drugs line became active again within hours of the pair being arrested. In its latest incarnation, Haider Ali, 34, who was known as 'The Ghost', was running the infamous drugs line, until he and two others were caught by police last year. Now they have been brought to jus When a CCTV operator spotted what appeared to be a drug deal in progress on Baron Street in Rochdale, officers followed a Nissan Qashqai car and when they swooped Ali ran away from the front passenger seat but was arrested a short distance away He had £1,000 in cash on him as well as wraps of cocaine and heroin in his pockets. On the dashboard in front of his seat police found 75 wraps of cocaine and 32 wraps of heroin

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Animals A 31-year-old cat lives in Stockport, her owner has revealed the secret to her long life Stockport resident Leslie Greenhough claims to have the world's oldest cat Comments News Miranda Pell Search and Discover Writer 17:16, 28 Jul 2026 View 4 A man who claims to have the world's oldest cat has revealed his secret to giving his furry friend a long, healthy life Leslie Greenhough, 71, from Stockport, believes his tortoiseshell Millie, born in 1995, is currently the oldest living feline at the age of 31 , which for cats is the equivalent of 146 human years Millie was first owned by Leslie's late wife, Paula, who got Millie the same year as a three-month-old kitten. evidence_packet.evidence_text: There is a moment in which Neill’s character, Cliff Buxton imparts some wisdom handed down by his wife: “Failure is never quite so frightening as regret” With those words in mind, I’m pleased to tell you that the Manchester Evening News has launched a campaign to secure the future of the Lovell Telescope at Jodrell Bank after financial backing for the e-Merlin telescope network was scrapped Much like the satellite at Parkes, the Lovell Telescope is also set in a charming, mid century, countryside outpost. But the beauty and quaintness of the UNESCO World Heritage Site belies its importance View 6 Images The Lovell telescope at the Jodrell Bank Observatory, in Cheshire as the sky changes colour at sunrise (Image: Peter Byrne/PA Wire) Standing since 1957, it’s the world's third largest steerable radio telescope and in 1966 intercepted and printed the first-ever pictures from the Moon's surface. It went on to play a key covert role in the Cold War For five years at the height of the tensions, Jodrell Bank was relied upon to give a four-minute warning of an impending nuclear attack

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A University of Salford student has launched a clothing brand inspired by her own journey with scoliosis after graduating. Sophie Whalley, 21, from Accrington, launched DailyMova to create her own solutions for the struggles she faced with the condition After finding a gap in the market, Sophie designed adaptable athleisure which looked stylish, felt comfortable, and supported asymmetrical bodies through extra padding, adjustable length materials, easy use clips and moveable straps She said: “For years, I’ve struggled to find activewear that is comfortable throughout the day. Too much compression on my ribs, not enough padding on my back and straps falling down. So rather than waiting for a fashion solution, I decided to create one myself.” “I’m just one person with scoliosis. There are so many more people out there with it, all with different needs.” “I never found anything that was suited directly for my body. So, it was really important that I created a brand that didn’t seem out of the ordinary, draw attention to the disability or make you look different from anyone else.” “DailyMova envisions all of that and is also a strong community-based brand where the girls involved help the design process but also feel supported as a group and movement.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The application related to a site off Hasty Lane Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council has refused permission in principle for up to nine homes on land off Hasty Lane in Hale Barns The application, submitted on behalf of Matthew Welch by Chorley-based MWT Planning, sought to establish the principle of residential development on a parcel of grassland adjacent to 1 Hasty Lane. The decision was issued under delegated powers on 22nd July Planners gave three reasons for refusal: the site's overlap with land safeguarded for HS2, its Green Belt location, and the density of the proposed development Part of the site fronting Hasty Lane sits on land formally safeguarded for Phase 2b of HS2's Crewe–Manchester route HS2 Ltd objected to the application, advising the council that the safeguarded land is required for infrastructure works including highway diversions and embankments, and that further parts of the site would be used as a construction compound and for woodland mitigation planting

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Matthew Torbitt worked for Bury South MP Christian Wakeford when, between August 2022 and September 2024, he claimed rail tickets that were "not for Parliamentary purposes", Thames Magistrates' Court heard He also admitted making a false claim for travel and accommodation expenses on 2 October 2024 Prosecutor Maisha Mannan told the court the claims totalled more than £6,000, according to an early estimate by the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), but the exact sum will be calculated at a later date Torbitt, who appeared in court dressed in a navy blue suit, pleaded guilty to two counts of fraud by false representation District Judge Navneet Sher sent the case to Snaresbrook Crown Court for sentence at a later date, which has yet to be fixed "It's unlikely to be before four weeks, in any event," she told the defendant

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.summary: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! […] The post Young Musician’s Summer School appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Young Musician’s Summer School . Young Musician’s Summer School. . Book here . . . . . . . Friday | 03.07.2026 . . . World of Music . Share . . . . --> . . We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club , or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! . . . . . Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. . . . . We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument.. . . Snacks and drinks provided, and pizzas on the final day. Please bring your own packed lunch to sessions Monday-Thursday.. . Dates: Monday 17th – Friday 21st August. Times: 10:00-16:30 Monday-Thursday, then a performance for friends and family on Friday at 13:00 (students will be expected to come in at 10:00 sharp on the Friday).. Ages: 12-18 years old. Cost: £150 for the full course. Bursaries are available for those on lower income – please email learning@bandonthewall.org to arrange this.. . Spaces are limited – Book here . . . Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

О том моменте, когда между людьми исчезают роли и, наконец, становится невозможно притворяться. На сцене — Алексей Панин и Ольга Силина. Тонкая актерская игра, живая энергия и удивительно узнаваемая история, в которой каждый услышит что-то своё. “Скамейка” — спектакль, после которого хочется немного помолчать и еще долго думать о главном. evidence_packet.lead: Fancy a space to connect with the community away from Canal Street?
evidence_packet.summary: Fancy a space to connect with the community away from Canal Street? Kiki Family Social is a relaxed, grassroots meet-up with no rigid expectations, pressure, or hierarchy
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fancy a space to connect with the community away from Canal Street? Kiki Family Social is a relaxed, grassroots meet-up with no rigid expectations, pressure, or hierarchy. The space is shaped by the people who come along — everyone helps make it what it is We meet every Thursday, and there’s always space at the table whether you’re new to Manchester or just dipping your toe into social meet-ups You’ll usually find a mix of familiar faces and new ones each week. We typically gather at a reserved table inside with pride flags, and there’s often a table outside too. On busy nights we’ll make sure flags are on the outside table as well. If you’re unsure where we are, just a 📅 Every Thursday, 7:30pm (You’re welcome to arrive earlier or later) 🍻 This isn’t a sober event, but there’s no pressure to drink. The bar offers zero-alcohol options as well as tea and coffee

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester City FC Memorabilia and 3am alarm calls - life as a Man City fan in Hong Kong and Korea Manchester City fans in Hong Kong and Korea share their history with the Blues and how they follow the team from thousands of miles away View 2 Images Hui Jeong Lee f Comments Sport Simon Bajkowski Chief Manchester City Writer 06:00, 29 Jul 2026 Manchester City fans in Hong Kong and South Korea have at least one thing in common: they're a lot more popular than they used to be. The success of other teams, coupled with Korean excitement at Park It was another player from the region that first attracted Cheng Hang Lun Eamonn to the Blues 21 years ago when he was in secondary school in Hong Kong. Picking a team on Pro Evo, he saw that 'Man Blue' had Chinese star Sun Jihai in their XI alongside a few other names he recogni A love story started there, even if it was mocked by his mates. "At that time my friends laughed at me as most of them were Man United or Liverpool fans. They just did not get why I would support a team with no champions," he tells the Manchester Evening News Get all the best Man City news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the MEN! "Back when I first started supporting them, City were barely even on the map for most Hong Kong football fans. You could barely find any official merchandise in local sports stores, and hardly any local bars would prioritise screening their matches unless it was a big cup tie."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: 17 октября 2026 года в Brixton Jamm состоится концерт Андрея Кравченко в Лондоне Андрей Кравченко покорил сердца тысяч слушателей благодаря своему уникальному голосу, харизме и способности превращать личные истории в песни, близкие каждому. Andy Burnham described it as the 'best day of my life' while addressing personnel at Heron House, close to Manchester's Albert Square, on Friday morning Addressing staff upon his arrival, Mr Burnham said: "I cannot tell you what a proud moment this is. I think this might be the best day of my life "I'm not joking. I know you think I am, but I'm not. Things are just completely coming full circle here, for me to be here with you all in the heart of Manchester this Friday morning at the end of a fairly big week is just everything to me." He continued: "Things are just completely coming full circle here for me, and to be here with you all in the heart of Manchester this Friday morning, at the end of a fairly big week, is just everything to me because it's almost exactly 35 years since I left this city as a recentl "That really is an experience that I've never forgotten, my generation of people growing up here. And it's true of places all over the country to get on in life, you had to leave where you where you were because things weren't here."
